title: Also shout out to their digital rush because I had a GREAT mezzanine ...
transcript: It's actually crazy how much better the replacement casts in cabaret have been compared to that original cast. I really was not a huge fan of this production back when I saw it with Eddie Redmayne and Gael Rankin. To me, both of their performances felt really flat. But I reluctantly went back and saw it with Adam Lambert and Alice Crivello and liked it a lot better with them in it. And now, having gone back to see Orville Peck and Eva Noblezada, I am happy to report that I liked them both just as much as I liked that previous cast. And the thing that I loved most about both of their performances is they're both giving radically different performances from anyone that's come before them. Orville Peck, MC leans into the sinister side of the character. He is immediately presenting himself as the villain of the piece. He even sometimes speaks in this really deep, demonic voice that I found really effective. This is in contrast to Eddie Redmayne, who just kind of played him as a creepy little guy who slowly becomes more sinister throughout the show, and Adam Lambert, who played the MC more as like an unwitting participant rather than someone who was inherently evil. And so it was really fun to watch Orville go in the complete opposite direction. And his voice sounds so good singing this score. Prior to this, I really didn't know who Orville Peck was, but I actually went Home and listened to a bunch of his music because of how much I liked him in the show, and I am now a fan. And then, of course, you have Eva Noblezada as Sally Bowles, who is just always so great in everything she does, and this is certainly no exception. He brings a real vulnerability to Sally Bowles that I've never really seen before. And on paper, this really shouldn't work, because Sally is a character that typically is so guarded and puts on this facade and this persona. And yet Eva still manages to put on that facade for other characters while letting us, the audience, see what lies underneath it. And it is just such a beautifully nuanced and moving performance. And of course, vocally, she just knocks it out of the park. In my opinion, it is the best this role has ever been sung. And so if you are considering going back to the club, going for your first time to see one of them, I really do recommend it. It is still not my favorite production of cabaret, but seeing these two in the leads, in my opinion, is totally worth it.
